newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine foreign loan law okay, says World Bank.
newsitem.headline: Philippine foreign loan law okay, says World Bank.

text.p: A World Bank official said on Tuesday a new Philippine law which seeks to favour local firms in consultancy and building contracts under projects funded by ODA loans was alright if it was implemented properly.
"Domestic contracts must really be given protection, as long as the protection is not excessive and it should not be there forever," WB resident representative Vinay Bhargava told a news conference.

The Japanese government, one of the Philippines' biggest donors under ODA (official development assistance), had complained about the provisions which prohibit hiring of foreign consultants in ODA-financed projects and give preference to Filipino contractors.
Philippine president Fidel Ramos had assured Japanese prime minister Ryutaro Hashimoto during their bilateral meeting last month the provision would be scrapped, but did not say when.

The World Bank is co-organising a pledging session in Tokyo next week to fund Philippine projects. The Philippines is hoping to get $2.55 billion in new commitments from bilateral and multilateral lending institutions during the meet.
